deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a page of German-language history notes, a school or lecture notebook, on Darius I and the opening of the Persian Wars. It continues the previous page (Cambyses, Pseudo-Smerdis, Darius' accession) and leads into the next (Marathon, Xerxes). The handwriting and the red-ink corrections suggest a pupil's exercise corrected by a teacher. Nothing suggests mathematical work by Gauss, and the page may not be in Gauss's hand at all.

Content, in order:
(1) End of Darius' Scythian campaign. The Scythians retreated ever deeper into the interior. For lack of water Darius had to turn back, but Thrace and Macedonia became tributary to him again.
(2) Aristagoras is named as instigator of the Greek (Ionian) revolt. '496' something (the first uprising or battle) was suppressed. Aristagoras became governor ('Statthalter') of Miletus.
(3) Darius then planned to attack the European Greeks, especially the Athenians.
(4) In 492 an expedition was fitted out and ended unhappily for the Persians. A large fleet with land troops was under Mardonius. Rounding Mount Athos, most of the fleet was destroyed by the north wind.
(5) In 490 a second fleet was assembled. At first the enterprise succeeded beyond expectation: the Sporades and Cyclades submitted without resistance. So did most cities of Greece proper except Sparta and Athens.
(6) With greater caution the Persians chose the best part of Attica as the theatre of war, leading to Marathon on the next page.

No derivation, formula or computation is present.
errors: Historical rather than mathematical slips: the chronology of the Ionian revolt is garbled.

The revolt ran 499–494 BC and ended with the fall of Miletus and the battle of Lade. '496' and the remark that Aristagoras 'became' governor of Miletus after the revolt are inaccurate; he was already deputy ruler of Miletus before it.
The 492 expedition and Mardonius' fleet wrecked at Athos are the same event. The notes present them as if they were two successive attempts.
The adjoining next page gives Marathon as 29 September 490. Modern estimates are usually August or September (often 12 September) 490 BC. This is not on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine school-level history notes with teacher-style red-ink corrections. It has no mathematical content and possibly is not even by Gauss.

checkable.asserts: The reign length of Darius I stated on the preceding page (522–486 BC = 36 years) is arithmetically consistent.
Two years separate the failed Mardonius expedition (492 BC) and the second expedition (490 BC), as the page's dates imply.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: the image shows 'für' with 'vor' written above as a correction. The intended reading is 'vor Mangel an Wasser'.
Line 3: 'Thrazien' carries a small red-ink correction mark in the image. The reading 'Thrazien und Mazedonien' is plausible.
Line 5: the word after 'die erste' is unclear in the image; 'Schlacht' is doubtful. The sense requires something like 'Empörung' or an uprising that was 'gedämpft'.
Line 17: the phrase after 'Cykladen im' is illegible in the image; the machine reading is uncertain. Sense: 'submitted without any resistance'.
Last line: 'von Attica' appears struck through, with 'Attica' written above in red ink. The intended reading is probably 'den besten Theil Attica's' / 'von Attica'.
Top-left margin, red ink: the note is a faint correction or annotation. The folio number '40' is in pencil.
